Has: rocky beach, resident-only parking, restroom, uneven access, dogs allowed off leash October 1-May 15, May 16-September 30 dogs allowed only 6am-10am and 5:30pm-sunset.
items.address: At the eastern end of Broad Street, Jamestown

items.name: Potter Cove Beach (Taylor Point)
items.blurb: This narrow beach follows Potter Cove just north of the Newport Bridge. Stairs from the lower parking area reach the shore while nearby rock outcrops provide views across the East Passage. Has: narrow beach, parking, stairs, restrooms at Taylor Point, dogs allowed off leash October 1-May 15, May 16-September 30 dogs allowed only 6am-10am and 5:30pm-sunset.
items.address: Bay View Drive and East Shore Road, Jamestown

items.name: Sheffield Cove shoreline
items.blurb: The head of Sheffield Cove has a cobble shore bordered by tidal marsh. It is a wildlife-viewing shoreline across the road from Mackerel Cove rather than a managed swimming beach. Has: cobble shore, salt marsh, birdwatching, nearby paid parking.
items.address: On the North side of Beavertail Road across the street from Mackerel Cove Beach, Jamestown

items.name: Spirketing Street cobble beach
items.blurb: Concrete steps descend from the street-end public path to a cobble beach. The shore faces the West Passage and offers sunset views. Has: cobble beach, steep steps, very limited parking, no restrooms.
items.address: At the intersection of Seaview Drive and Spirketing Street, Jamestown

items.name: Briggs Beach
items.blurb: Briggs is an ocean beach associated with a private beach club. The town identifies its facilities as available to members rather than general visitors. Has: private beach club, members only.

items.name: Goosewing Beach
items.blurb: A beach and nature preserve reached on foot from South Shore Beach. Respect nesting-bird closures and marked habitat boundaries.

items.name: Goosewing Beach (Quicksand Pond barrier)
items.blurb: Goosewing is the sandy barrier beach beside Quicksand Pond and a protected bird habitat. Visitors walk in from the adjoining South Shore Beach parking area. Has: barrier beach, wildlife habitat, seasonal nesting closures, adjacent paid parking, portable restrooms at South Shore Beach, dogs prohibited April 1-Labor Day.
items.address: Access through South Shore Beach, 140 South Shore Beach Road, Little Compton
items.hours: Daylight hours year-round; nesting areas restricted seasonally. · South Shore lot charges approximately Memorial Day-Labor Day: $25 weekdays or $30 weekends, collected 8am-4pm.

items.name: High Hill Marsh eastern barrier beach
items.blurb: High Hill Marsh eastern barrier beach is named in the state’s coastal-barrier inventory. Current public entry arrangements have not been confirmed. Has: coastal barrier.

items.name: Lloyd's Beach
items.blurb: The town's comprehensive plan identifies Lloyd's as a privately owned beach with resident access. Current admission arrangements should be confirmed with the owner before visiting. Has: private beach, resident access identified in town plan.

items.name: Long Pond Beach
items.blurb: Long Pond Beach is named in the state’s coastal-barrier inventory. Current public entry arrangements have not been confirmed. Has: coastal barrier.

items.name: Round Meadow Pond barrier beach
items.blurb: Round Meadow Pond barrier beach is named in the state’s coastal-barrier inventory. Current public entry arrangements have not been confirmed. Has: coastal barrier.

items.name: Round Pond Beach
items.blurb: Round Pond Beach is named in the state’s coastal-barrier inventory. Current public entry arrangements have not been confirmed. Has: coastal barrier.

items.name: Sakonnet Harbor Beach
items.blurb: A small beach and launch ramp border the sheltered basin at Sakonnet Point. It provides harbor access rather than a developed swimming facility. Has: harbor beach, boat ramp, parking, no restrooms.
items.address: On the north side of Sakonnet Point Road at the base of the harbor, Little Compton

items.name: Ship Pond Cove barrier beach
items.blurb: Ship Pond Cove barrier beach is named in the state’s coastal-barrier inventory. Current public entry arrangements have not been confirmed. Has: coastal barrier.

items.name: South Shore Beach
items.blurb: South Shore is Little Compton's public Atlantic-facing beach beside Tunipus Pond. Walking east connects it with the Goosewing preserve shoreline. Has: sand and cobble beach, seasonal lifeguards, parking, portable restrooms.
items.address: 140 South Shore Beach Road, Little Compton
items.hours: Parking gate opens 8am; seasonal fee collection 8am-4pm approximately Memorial Day-Labor Day. Summer lifeguards. · Visitor parking $25 weekdays or $30 weekends/holidays; resident stickers available.

items.name: Taylor's Lane Beach (Church Bay)
items.blurb: A short dirt path reaches a sand-and-cobble beach on Church Bay. The view extends toward the mouth of the Sakonnet River and Sachuest Point. Has: sand and cobble beach, limited parking, no restrooms.
items.address: West end of Taylor's Lane, Little Compton

items.name: Town Landing Beach (Grange Avenue)
items.blurb: A grassy town parcel overlooks a rocky beach at the end of Grange Avenue. A short dirt path descends from the picnic area to the shore. Has: rocky beach, parking, picnic tables, uneven access.
items.address: End of Grange Avenue, Little Compton

items.name: Town Way Beach
items.blurb: A street-end path descends to a cobble beach on the Sakonnet River. At low tide the shoreline extends toward Almy's Creek and its marsh. Has: cobble beach, limited street parking, no restrooms, tidal access.
items.address: At the western end of Town Way, Little Compton

items.name: Warren's Point Beach (Tappens Beach)
items.blurb: Warren's Point has a private club beach on Little Compton's south coast. The town's plan identifies access through club membership. Has: private beach club, members only.

items.name: Watch House Pond Beach
items.blurb: Watch House Pond Beach is named in the state’s coastal-barrier inventory. Current public entry arrangements have not been confirmed. Has: coastal barrier.

items.name: Atlantic Beach (Middletown)
items.blurb: Atlantic Beach occupies the Middletown end of the sandy shoreline on Easton Bay. Dunlap-Wheeler Park sits beside its eastern approach. Has: sandy beach, nearby park, limited parking, no on-site restrooms.

items.name: Kingfisher Avenue / Peckham Avenue beach
items.blurb: A long public path descends toward a cobble beach on the Sakonnet River. Large shoreline rocks and uneven footing characterize this small access. Has: cobble beach, limited parking, no restrooms, rugged path.
items.address: At the intersection of Indian Avenue and Peckham Avenue, Middletown

items.name: Peabody's Beach
items.blurb: Peabody's is a privately operated beach at the northern end of the Third Beach shoreline. A designated public right-of-way also provides pedestrian access beside the facility. Has: sandy beach, seasonal lifeguards, parking, snack facility, public pedestrian right-of-way.
items.hours: 2026: weekends/holidays May 25-June 18; daily from June 19; beach 9am-7pm and lifeguards 9am-5pm. Public entry ends 5pm; lot locks 7pm. · 2026 parking $30 weekdays or $45 weekends/holidays; member parking included with membership.

items.name: Sachuest Beach (Second Beach)
items.blurb: Sachuest is a long Atlantic-facing beach with a broad sandy shoreline. Surfer's End is the western part of this same beach and has its own parking restrictions. Has: sandy beach, seasonal lifeguards, parking, restrooms, showers, changing area, concessions.
items.hours: Memorial Day weekend-Labor Day weekend 8am-5pm; main parking gate closes 9pm. · From July 1 2026: daily car parking $30 weekdays or $40 weekends/holidays. Season pass: Middletown $100; nonresident $200; senior resident $85; senior nonresident $170. Walk-ons: no charge. Surfer's End lot is resident-pass-only.

items.name: Sachuest Point rocky and cobble shore
items.blurb: The refuge occupies the point between Second Beach and the Sakonnet River. Its coastal trails reach views of a rocky and cobble shoreline managed for wildlife. Has: rocky and cobble shore, parking, visitor center restrooms, wildlife habitat, dogs prohibited.

items.name: Shore Drive cobble beach
items.blurb: A short path from Shore Drive reaches a small cobble beach. The approach is rocky and roadside parking is prohibited. Has: cobble beach, no street parking, no restrooms, uneven access.

items.name: Third Beach
items.blurb: Third Beach faces the mouth of the Sakonnet River and generally has less surf than Second Beach. The beach includes a boat-ramp area and a designated swimming area. Has: sandy beach, seasonal lifeguards, resident-only seasonal parking, portable restrooms, boat ramp, picnic tables, leashed dogs May 1-September 30 only 5am-7:45am.
items.hours: Memorial Day weekend-Labor Day weekend 8am-5pm. · Walk-ons: no charge. Seasonal parking is resident-pass-only; resident season pass $100 or $85 for residents age 65+.

items.name: Wolcott Avenue rocky beach
items.blurb: An overgrown path from Wolcott Avenue reaches the rocky shore of Easton Bay. Uneven terrain makes this a rugged shoreline access. Has: rocky beach, rugged path, limited nearby street parking, no restrooms.
items.address: At the intersection of Tuckerman Avenue and Wolcott Avenue, Middletown

items.name: Salty Brine State Beach
items.blurb: A compact beach near the fishing docks, seafood restaurants, and Block Island ferry terminal.

items.name: Black Point rocky coves
items.blurb: The Black Point fishing area has a boulder-strewn shoreline and tide pools. A wooded path from Ocean Road connects several small coastal inlets. Has: rocky coves, trailhead parking, fishing access, uneven terrain.

items.name: Bonnet Shores Beach Club beach
items.blurb: This condominium beach club occupies a privately managed section of the Bonnet Shores waterfront. Members and authorized guests enter through the club’s facilities. Has: private beach club, member or guest authorization required, lifeguards, pets prohibited.

items.name: Calef Avenue cobble beach
items.blurb: A grass right-of-way reaches the seawall above a cobble beach near Point Judith. Reaching the shore involves rough rock surfaces. Has: cobble beach, rocky access, no restrooms.
items.address: At the intersection of Calef Avenue and Louise Avenue, Narragansett

items.name: Camp Cronin Beach and Point Judith breakwater
items.blurb: A rocky beach and shoreline border the fishermen’s memorial at Point Judith. The site also provides access to the eastern Harbor of Refuge breakwater. Has: rocky shoreline, parking, seasonal portable restrooms, fishing access, uneven access.
items.hours: Parking: no charge.

items.name: Galilee Beach Club beach
items.blurb: Galilee Beach Club maintains a private section of the Sand Hill Cove shoreline. Beach access through the club is reserved for members and their guests. Has: private beach club, members and authorized guests only.

items.name: Kelly Beach (Bonnet Shores)
items.blurb: Kelly Beach is the ocean-facing community beach at Bonnet Shores. District beach tags identify residents and authorized visitors. Has: resident and authorized guest beach, beach tag required, dogs prohibited during official open hours.

items.name: Little Beach (Bonnet Shores)
items.blurb: Little Beach is a separate Bonnet Shores community waterfront on the bay side. District access rules apply to residents and their authorized visitors. Has: resident and authorized guest beach, beach tag required, dogs prohibited during official open hours, no lifeguards.
items.address: Northern Colonel John Gardner Road, Narragansett

items.name: Narragansett Town Beach
items.blurb: This broad sandy beach fronts the ocean beside Narragansett's town center. The town charges separately for seasonal daytime beach admission and parking. Has: sandy beach, seasonal lifeguards, restrooms, showers, changing rooms, concessions, accessible mats and beach chairs.
items.hours: 2026: Memorial Day weekend then daily May 30-September 7. Admission gates 8:30am-5pm weekdays or 7:30am-5pm weekends/holidays; lifeguards until 6pm. · 2026 daily admission $12; ages 11 and under no charge. Parking $10 weekdays or $15 weekends/holidays plus sales tax; credit-card fee 2.95%. Resident/taxpayer season parking $50. Nonresidents use West Lot; South Lot may admit nonresidents after 1pm weekdays. Off-season beach admission: no charge.

items.name: Pilgrim Avenue cobble beach
items.blurb: The public extension of Pilgrim Avenue reaches a cobble beach north of Point Judith. This is a small shoreline access without developed visitor facilities. Has: cobble beach, limited street parking, no restrooms, uneven access.
items.address: At the eastern end of Pilgrim Avenue, Narragansett

items.name: Roger W. Wheeler State Beach
items.blurb: A family-oriented beach with a playground and seasonal amenities near Point Judith.

items.name: Roger Wheeler State Beach (Sand Hill Cove)
items.blurb: Roger Wheeler lies inside the Point Judith Harbor of Refuge. The breakwater shelters its sandy swimming beach from much of the open-ocean surf. Has: sandy beach, seasonal lifeguards, restrooms, showers, parking, playground, concessions.
items.hours: Year-round shore access. 2026 staffed season May 23-September 7; lifeguards 9am-6pm weekdays and 8:30am-6pm weekends/holidays, subject to staffing and weather. No lifeguards after September 7. · 2026 parking: RI vehicles $6 weekdays or $7 weekends/holidays; out-of-state vehicles $12 weekdays or $14 weekends/holidays. Season pass: RI $30; nonresident $60. Age 65+: half-price. Off-season parking: no charge.

items.name: Salty Brine State Beach (Galilee Beach)
items.blurb: This small sandy beach sits beside the entrance to Galilee harbor. Visitors can watch fishing boats and ferries pass close to the shore. Has: sandy beach, seasonal lifeguards, restrooms, showers, parking, boardwalk, concessions.
items.hours: Year-round shore access. 2026 staffed season begins May 23; weekend-only service from the third weekend in August through September 7. Lifeguards 9am-6pm weekdays or 8:30am-6pm weekends/holidays when staffed; none after September 7. · 2026 parking: RI vehicles $6 weekdays or $7 weekends/holidays; out-of-state vehicles $12 weekdays or $14 weekends/holidays. Season pass: RI $30; nonresident $60. Age 65+: half-price. Off-season parking: no charge.

items.name: Scarborough North State Beach
items.blurb: Scarborough North is a broad ocean beach backed by a large pavilion and boardwalk. It forms the northern portion of the combined Scarborough shoreline. Has: sandy beach, seasonal lifeguards, restrooms, showers, parking, pavilions, concessions.
items.hours: Year-round shore access. 2026 staffed season begins May 23; weekend-only service from the third weekend in August through September 7. Lifeguards 9am-6pm weekdays or 8:30am-6pm weekends/holidays when staffed; none after September 7. · 2026 parking: RI vehicles $6 weekdays or $7 weekends/holidays; out-of-state vehicles $12 weekdays or $14 weekends/holidays. Season pass: RI $30; nonresident $60. Age 65+: half-price. Off-season parking: no charge.

items.name: Scarborough South State Beach
items.blurb: Scarborough South occupies the former Olivo's and Lido's beach properties beside Scarborough North. It has its own seasonal facilities and a shorter staffing season. Has: sandy beach, seasonal lifeguards subject to staffing, restrooms, showers, parking, pavilions, accessible beach chairs.
items.hours: Year-round shore access. Published 2026 amenity season begins June 20; daily service ends in August with late-season service subject to staffing. Seasonal lifeguards 9am-6pm weekdays or 8:30am-6pm weekends/holidays when staffed; none after September 7. · 2026 parking: RI vehicles $6 weekdays or $7 weekends/holidays; out-of-state vehicles $12 weekdays or $14 weekends/holidays. Season pass: RI $30; nonresident $60. Age 65+: half-price. Off-season parking: no charge.

items.name: South Ferry Beach
items.blurb: The end of South Ferry Road reaches a small cobble beach on the West Passage. The shoreline overlooks Dutch Island and Jamestown beside the university's bay campus. Has: cobble beach, no lifeguards, parking, portable restroom, kayak launch.
items.address: Located to the east of 220 S Ferry Road, Narragansett

items.name: The Dunes Club beach
items.blurb: The Dunes Club occupies a privately managed section of the Narragansett oceanfront. Its beach facilities serve club members and authorized guests. Has: private beach club, members and authorized guests only.

items.name: Whale Rock Beach
items.blurb: A woodland trail reaches a rocky beach overlooking Rhode Island Sound. The route includes boardwalk and uneven stretches through coastal habitat. Has: rocky beach, trail access, parking, uneven footing.

items.name: Fred Benson Town Beach
items.blurb: A town-operated beach along Crescent Beach, with seasonal concessions, rentals, and visitor facilities.

items.name: Mohegan Bluffs
items.blurb: A dramatic coastal overlook above the Atlantic. Check stairway and beach-access notices; erosion has caused restrictions at the bottom of the stairs. Access notice: https://dem.ri.gov/press-releases/bottom-mohegan-bluffs-staircase-block-island-closed-until-further-notice-due-erosion

items.name: Andy's Way Beach
items.blurb: A dirt-and-sand approach reaches the eastern shore of Great Salt Pond. The shallow shoreline is a well-known place for walking and shellfishing. Has: salt-pond beach, limited parking, bike racks.
items.address: South of 642 Corn Neck Road, New Shoreham

items.name: Baby Beach
items.blurb: Baby Beach is a small part of the Crescent Beach shoreline near town. The tourism council identifies it as a favored beach for children. Has: sandy beach.

items.name: Black Rock Beach
items.blurb: Black Rock is an exposed beach on the southern coast of Block Island. It is known locally as a surfing location. Has: rocky beach, surfing.

items.name: Block Island Boat Basin public launching beach
items.blurb: A small beach beside the harbormaster’s office provides access to Great Salt Pond. It serves as a public launching place for hand-carried boats. Has: small salt-pond beach, kayak launch, parking, marina restrooms.

items.name: Charlestown Beach (Block Island)
items.blurb: A west-side path reaches this beach beside the entrance to Great Salt Pond. The shore is known for sunset views and fishing access. Has: beach, limited parking, sunset views.

items.name: Clay Head Beach
items.blurb: A trail through fields and shrubs reaches a small beach beneath the northeastern bluffs. The beach can be rocky after strong surf and is part of a longer coastal walking route. Has: rocky beach, trail access, parking, bike racks.
items.address: Entrance next to 728 Corn Neck Road, New Shoreham

items.name: Coast Guard Beach
items.blurb: This beach lies beside the channel into Great Salt Pond near the former Coast Guard station. Passing boats and tidal currents characterize the shoreline. Has: channel-side beach, strong tidal currents.
items.address: End of Coast Guard Road near the former Coast Guard station, New Shoreham

items.name: Cooneymus Cove Beach
items.blurb: A sandy path at the end of Cooneymus Road reaches a cobble beach on the island's southwest side. The cove offers a quiet shoreline for walking and sunset views. Has: cobble beach, limited street parking, bike rack.
items.address: At western most end of Cooneymus Road, New Shoreham

items.name: Cow Cove and North Light beach
items.blurb: A cobble shoreline runs from Settlers Rock toward North Light and Sandy Point. The northern tip has dangerous currents and is not a swimming destination. Has: sand and cobble beach, limited parking, wildlife habitat, dangerous currents.
items.address: At the northern most end of Corn Neck Road, New Shoreham

items.name: Dinghy Beach (Mosquito Beach)
items.blurb: This beach-and-marsh parcel borders the southeast side of Great Salt Pond. A boardwalk reaches the shore used by small boats and shellfishers. Has: salt-pond beach, limited parking, boardwalk, no ramp from boardwalk to sand.
items.address: Southwest of 1734 Corn Neck Road, New Shoreham

items.name: Dorry's Cove Beach
items.blurb: Dorry’s Cove is a separate small beach on the island’s west coast. The sheltered-looking cove forms part of Block Island’s rugged western shoreline. Has: cove beach, undeveloped shoreline.

items.name: Fred Benson Town Beach (Crescent Beach)
items.blurb: Fred Benson is the town's managed swimming beach along the larger Crescent Beach shoreline. The pavilion provides the island's main concentration of public beach services. Has: sandy beach, seasonal lifeguards, parking, restrooms, showers, changing rooms, concessions.
items.hours: Summer lifeguards.

items.name: Grace's Cove Beach
items.blurb: Grace’s Cove is one of the secluded beaches on Block Island’s western coast. Its setting is suited to coastal walks and sunset views. Has: cove beach, undeveloped shoreline.

items.name: Mansion Beach
items.blurb: Mansion Beach lies below the bluffs at the end of Mansion Road. A sandy lane reaches the beach and its parking area. Has: sandy beach, parking, bike racks.
items.address: At the Eastern end of Mansion Road, New Shoreham

items.name: Mohegan Bluffs Beach
items.blurb: A long wooden stairway descends below the island's high southern bluffs. The beach has dramatic coastal views and a strenuous return climb. Has: beach below cliffs, long staircase, parking, bike racks, uneven final descent.

items.name: Ocean View Park beach access
items.blurb: The former hotel site has coastal paths and a pavilion above the ocean. A steep approach provides beach access near Old Harbor. Has: beach access, steep path, pavilion, coastal views.

items.name: Scotch Beach
items.blurb: Scotch Beach is a sandy section of the Crescent Beach shoreline north of the town pavilion. A short approach from Corn Neck Road reaches the beach and a small parking area. Has: sandy beach, limited parking, nearby town-beach facilities.
items.address: At the intersection of Scotch Beach Road and Corn Neck Road, New Shoreham

items.name: Surf Beach
items.blurb: Surf Beach occupies the southern end of Crescent Beach below the former Surf Hotel. Its rocky patches make it a recognized snorkeling location. Has: sand and rocky shoreline, snorkeling.

items.name: Vaill Beach (Vail Beach)
items.blurb: Vaill Beach lies below a coastal hollow near Painted Rock. A steep path reaches a secluded shore with rocks and strong surf. Has: rocky beach, steep trail, rough surf.
items.address: Path from Snake Hole Road near Painted Rock, New Shoreham

items.name: West Beach (Block Island)
items.blurb: West Beach has a mixture of sand and cobbles along Block Island Sound. Its road-end access offers a quieter shoreline for walking and beachcombing. Has: sand and cobble beach, no lifeguards, limited street parking.

items.name: Ann Street Pier cobble beach
items.blurb: A small cobble beach adjoins the public dinghy pier at Ann Street. Nearby maritime facilities serve harbor visitors and ferry passengers. Has: cobble beach, public pier, nearby paid parking, nearby restrooms and showers.

items.name: Bailey's Beach (Spouting Rock Beach Association)
items.blurb: Bailey's is a private club beach on Newport's south coast. Club facilities are restricted to members and their authorized guests. Has: private beach club, members and authorized guests only.

items.name: Brenton Point State Park rocky shore
items.blurb: Brenton Point has an exposed rocky shoreline with tide pools at the entrance to Narragansett Bay. A coastal walking route and large picnic lawns overlook the water. Has: rocky shoreline, parking, seasonal restrooms, picnic areas, accessible park paths.
items.hours: Parking: no charge.

items.name: Castle Hill Beach
items.blurb: Castle Hill Inn maintains this private sandy beach beside its seaside accommodations. Summer attendants provide beach seating and umbrellas for guests. Has: private guest beach, beach attendants, chairs and umbrellas, dogs prohibited on beach.
items.hours: Beach year-round; 2026 attendants 10am-6pm daily May 1-September 7 and weekends September 11-October 12.

items.name: Cherry Street rocky beach
items.blurb: Steep steps at the end of Cherry Street reach a narrow rocky beach. The shoreline is a small neighborhood access off Washington Street. Has: rocky beach, steep steps, street parking, no restrooms.
items.address: At the western end of Cherry street, Newport

items.name: Easton's Beach (First Beach)
items.blurb: Easton's Beach follows the Atlantic shore beside the northern entrance to Newport's Cliff Walk. Its broad sand and boardwalk make it one of the city's principal public beaches. Has: sandy beach, boardwalk, seasonal lifeguards, restrooms, parking, dogs prohibited Memorial Day weekend-September 30.
items.hours: Lifeguards Memorial Day-Labor Day. Parking lots 9am-9pm weekdays and 8am-9pm weekends/holidays. · 2026 parking April 1-November 30: $25 weekdays or $35 weekends/holidays plus 7% tax. December 1-March 31: no charge. Newport residential parking sticker holders: no charge. Nonresident season permit $150; age 65+ $100.

items.name: Fort Adams State Park Beach
items.blurb: This small harbor-facing beach sits within Fort Adams State Park. Its setting provides views of Newport Harbor and nearby sailing activity. Has: harbor beach, parking, restrooms, showers, seasonal swimming area, dogs prohibited in designated swim areas April 1-September 30 except service animals, leashed dogs allowed outside that restriction.
items.hours: Seasonal lifeguards subject to staffing; DEM reported no lifeguards for Labor Day weekend 2026. · Beach access and ordinary parking: no charge.

items.name: Gooseberry Beach
items.blurb: Gooseberry occupies a sheltered cove along Ocean Avenue. The privately operated beach offers paid visitor access under the operator's entry rules. Has: sandy beach, seasonal lifeguards, paid parking, restrooms, showers, changing rooms, concessions.
items.hours: Daily in season 9am-5pm; lifeguards 9am-5pm; snack facility 11am-5pm, weather permitting. · 2026 nonmember parking: $30 weekdays or $40 weekends/holidays plus 7% tax; online service/transaction fees may apply. Bikes/e-bikes/scooters $10. Operator prohibits walk-ons and drop-offs.

items.name: Hazard's Beach
items.blurb: Hazard's is a privately managed beach along Newport's ocean shoreline. Access to its club facilities requires membership or guest authorization. Has: private beach club, members and authorized guests only.

items.name: King Park Beach
items.blurb: A small beach borders the waterfront lawn at King Park. It is close to picnic space and a boat-launch area on Newport Harbor. Has: small beach, street parking, restrooms, playground, picnic area, kayak launch.

items.name: King's Beach and Fishing Access
items.blurb: This rocky cove lies beside Price's Neck on Newport's south shore. It is a state fishing access with a small beach and rough shoreline. Has: rocky beach, parking, no restrooms, fishing access, uneven shore.
items.address: West of Prices Neck Road off of Ocean Avenue, Newport

items.name: Marine Avenue Beach
items.blurb: The Marine Avenue right-of-way leads to a cobble beach beside the Cliff Walk. It provides a small shoreline stopping place below the surrounding coastal properties. Has: cobble beach, limited street parking, no restrooms, uneven access.
items.address: At the intersection of Wetmore Avenue and Marine Avenue, Newport

items.name: Reject's Beach (public end of Bailey's Beach)
items.blurb: This small public beach lies beside the private Bailey's Beach club. It is reached at the southern end of the Cliff Walk. Has: sandy beach, public pedestrian access.
items.address: Southern end of Bellevue Avenue and Cliff Walk, Newport

items.name: Rose Island lighthouse beaches
items.blurb: Two beaches beside the lighthouse remain within the permitted visitor area during nesting season. Other parts of the island become accessible after the seasonal wildlife restrictions end. Has: island beaches, boat access only, no lifeguards, wildlife sanctuary, seasonal access restrictions.
items.hours: Public day visits May 16-October 12, 10am-4pm; nesting restrictions March 1-August 15. · Landing fee required; included with operator boat or ferry transport and waived for members.

items.name: Storer Park Beach
items.blurb: A sandy beach borders Storer Park just north of the Goat Island causeway. The park connects harbor views with a public pier and walking paths. Has: sandy beach, street parking, no restrooms, kayak launch, accessible park paths, leashed dogs allowed.
items.address: At the intersection of Washington Street and Bridge Street, Newport
items.hours: 6am-9pm

items.name: Walnut Street beach
items.blurb: The Walnut Street right-of-way reaches a small sandy beach on Newport's harbor shoreline. Concrete steps and a grassy approach provide access for pedestrians and hand-carried boats. Has: sandy beach, steps, street parking, no restrooms.
items.address: At the western end of Walnut Street, Newport

items.name: Bissel Cove shoreline and barrier beach
items.blurb: Bissel Cove connects a sheltered tidal inlet with the West Passage. The public access at Worsley Avenue reaches its rocky shoreline. Has: rocky shoreline, cove, hand-carried boat access.
items.address: At the eastern end of Worsley Avenue, North Kingstown

items.name: Blue Beach

items.hours: Approximately April 15-November 30; sunrise-sunset. · No charge.

items.name: Calf Pasture Point Beach
items.blurb: The Calf Pasture shoreline combines a long beach with coastal habitat near Allen Harbor. Visitors reach it on foot or by bicycle along the North Kingstown path system. Has: beach, walking and cycling access, trailhead parking, trailhead portable restrooms.
items.hours: No charge.

items.name: Camp Grosvenor beach
items.blurb: Camp Grosvenor has a swimming waterfront on the tidal Pettaquamscutt River. Access is associated with the camp’s programs rather than general beach admission. Has: estuary beach, camp access only.

items.name: Casey Point barrier beach
items.blurb: Casey Point barrier beach is named in the state’s coastal-barrier inventory. Current public entry arrangements have not been confirmed. Has: coastal barrier.

items.name: Compass Rose Beach
items.blurb: Compass Rose is a sandy beach on the south side of Quonset. Its shoreline and picnic area face the West Passage and Jamestown Bridge. Has: sandy beach, parking, seasonal portable restrooms, picnic tables, no lifeguards, leashed dogs allowed.
items.hours: Approximately April 15-November 30; sunrise-sunset.

items.name: Greene Point barrier beach
items.blurb: Greene Point barrier beach is named in the state’s coastal-barrier inventory. Current public entry arrangements have not been confirmed. Has: coastal barrier.

items.name: King Preserve Narrow River beach
